html:
Nadleh Whut'en is a First Nation of the Dakelh (Carrier) people at the east end of Fraser Lake in central British Columbia. Their name refers to the place where the salmon run up the Nautley River into the lake.

The Dakelh are Athabaskan speakers who lived by salmon fishing, hunting and trapping. In 1806 Simon Fraser of the North West Company built a trading post, later Fort Fraser, on their land. Their neighbours include Stellat'en, Lheidli T'enneh and Yekooche.
